questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Yemen?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Yemen on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Yemen article.

questions.proof: It borders Saudi Arabia and Oman on the north and the east.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Yemen?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Yemen article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “As of February _____, Yemen is divided into twenty governorates and one municipality called "Amanat Al-Asemah".”

hints.nudge: All four are years. Only one of them fits what the article says happened.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Governorates” part of the Yemen article.

questions.proof: As of February 2004, Yemen is divided into twenty governorates and one municipality called "Amanat Al-Asemah".

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “War continued, with Saudi Arabia and _____ supporting different sides.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “supporting”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Yemen article, under the heading “Government”.

questions.proof: War continued, with Saudi Arabia and Iran supporting different sides.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Men whose ancestors came from Yemen ruled Al-Andalus (Muslim _____) for centuries.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Muslim”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Yemen article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Men whose ancestors came from Yemen ruled Al-Andalus (Muslim Spain) for centuries.
